flows.description: Local append serializes the logical body and predecessor identities; no route-limit inference.
Direct claim insert: body, predecessors and identifiers; bound parameters enter claims.
Blob promotion copies staged bytes to durable graph storage without changing logical identity.
Immutable blob bytes are independently variable values; retain digest/length/promotion semantics.
Document API/local producer body, identity and predecessors reach the common claim writer.
Exchange importer delegates admission and projection; wire/decompression bounds are not a universal stored-cell cap.
Local sealing serializes admitted history into exact signed raw envelopes; body/wire representations both matter.
Legacy staged blob migration/copy may contain valid historical large cells.
Replication admission: raw CBOR, claim body, dependencies, blobs and signed metadata must retain exact identity.
Private physical clone preserves existing cells without passing per-kind/network producer validation.
Public copy/proof path includes clone/VACUUM fallback and all historical values; no import cap may reject them.
Physical row deletion may free a whole overflow chain; cooperative chunk checks cannot split a statement.
Tombstone identities, keys and dependency metadata need generation-aware visibility and evidence.
Finish/rollback/redelete, digest and finalizer work remain accounted; cached digest summary is not a full claim scan.
Historical proof restore/adoption must preserve exact full logical source, not only current routes.
Exact-adoption/trim publication and durable cleanup must be separated without bypassing certification.
Offline backup restore is a historical producer/open path; write-preserving recovery and opener quiescence require a separate plan.
Application admission passes actor/body/dependency values to Core and projection; guards cover raw legacy paths too.
Event positions/publication must retain canonical pointer/body and ordering semantics.
Backup import permits valid historical records under its own record/page limits, not client extractor limits.
